subject: Bespoke uptime rider + order form language request
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@atlantishealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@atlantishealth.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Apr 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: bespoke uptime rider + order form language

Hi Rafael —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and engineering here at Atlantis reviewed the standard MSA/SOW and we have two asks before we can route to Legal: a bespoke uptime/latency rider (we're calling it an "assurance rider") and a small set of order form clauses to lock in committed capacity and a regional failover guarantee.

High-level asks:
- Uptime: 99.95% monthly availability target for our production tenant in us-west, with a graduated credit schedule for partial breaches (we attached our preferred credit ladder).
- Latency: 95th-percentile tail for text-generation (1-2k token seq) and embeddings to meet < 250ms for embeddings and < 450ms for generation in normal operating conditions; want an explicit SLO for the 95th.
- Evidence: periodic telemetry snapshots and a quarterly evidence package (SRE runbook + uptime reports).
- Order form: committed baseline GPU capacity (dedicated pool), surge billing rules, and a clause for geo-failover pathing + notification obligations.

I've attached our redlined MSA and a short order-form template. Can Redwood provide: (1) a draft assurance rider that maps Redwood credits to our ladder, (2) proposed order-form language for committed capacity and failover, and (3) a list of audit artifacts you can supply?

We'd like to get a draft back by next Monday (30 Apr) so procurement can start routing. If it's easier, happy to take a 30-min call this week to align.

Thanks —
Ellen Park
Director, Cloud Integrations
Atlantis Health
ellen.park@atlantishealth.com
+1 415-555-0172

Attachments: Atlantis_MSA_redlines_20280420.pdf, orderform-draft-v1.docx

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@atlantishealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Apr 2028 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: bespoke uptime rider + order form language

Hi Ellen —

Really appreciate the clear asks and the redlines — that's very helpful. I'm looping in Kim (legal/procurement) and Marissa (customer ops) so we can move a complete package back to you. Quick reply with a proposed path: 

1) Draft rider: we'll convert your credit ladder into Redwood's rider format and propose equivalent availability buckets (we can do either a simple credit-per-minute or a graduated percentage schedule).
2) Latency SLOs: Product needs a couple data points (peak qps, typical sequence lengths, and % of requests that are embeddings vs. generation) to validate the numbers you requested. For example, embeddings <= 250ms at p95 is feasible at your committed baseline; at burst it may require burst capacity or wider tolerance.
3) Evidence & telemetry: we can provide quarterly telemetry snapshots (CSV + perf dashboard link) and a SOC2-based evidence bundle. We'll outline exactly which logs/metrics we can share and what requires a redaction/NDAs.
4) Order form language: we'll author committed-capacity language that ties billing to a baseline and defines surge increments; also propose a regional failover notification process (48-hour notice + automatic failover if regional outage > 12 hours).

Next steps: if you can send the peak qps and a short traffic profile (sample day or week), I'll have a first draft rider + order-form language by EOD Thu (26 Apr). If that timeline doesn't work for procurement, let me know and we'll prioritize.

Also attaching a basic uptime-rider template to show format so procurement can see where the credits map.

Best,
Rafael
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com
+1 650-555-0188

Attachments: uptime-rider-template.docx

Subject: Re: Request: bespoke uptime rider + order form language

Hi Ellen / Rafael —

Thanks for the note. A couple of practical points from Legal/Procurement before we draft final language: 

- We typically avoid hard latency guarantees tied to public internet variables, but we can agree a measurable SLO at our service ingress (Redwood -> customer tenant) with defined measurement scope (p95 computed on Redwood-facing telemetry for requests that originated within the specified region).
- For availability credits, acceptable approaches: a) credits expressed as % of monthly fees, b) credits bucketed by small time windows (minutes lost -> credit). We'll map your ladder to both formats so procurement can pick.
- Order form: we'll propose a committed baseline + contractual burst policy (burst allowed up to X% above baseline for N hours/day with an agreed surge price). Need to confirm the committed baseline in GPU units (e.g., 8xA100 equiv).
- Evidence: we can supply telemetry exports, dashboard links, and aggregated availability reports. Raw logs that contain customer data will require an evidence access NDA; telemetry/perf summaries are OK under the MSA.

Two asks for Atlantis:
1) Confirm the committed baseline in GPU units (or provide expected average concurrent inference threads).
2) Confirm whether you need an on-call escalation contact and a 24/7 paging commitment for production incidents (that has cost/ops implications).

If you can answer those two, we'll produce a formal "assurance rider" draft and order-form language for review. Rafael — I'm happy to take point on redline-ready language; Marissa and I will coordinate the execution steps (DocuSign path + procurement contacts).

Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Thanks Rafael / Kim —

Quick answers:
- Committed baseline: equivalent to 12xA100 (we can provide the exact instance mix if helpful).
- Traffic profile: attached is a sample week (avg QPS 42, peak 480 during a scheduled rundown). ~65% of requests are generation, 35% embeddings. Typical sequence length 300-1,800 tokens.
- On-call: yes, we'd like a 24/7 escalation for Sev1 incidents for production; tell us the incremental cost and we'll include it in procurement.

We'll plan a 30-min alignment call tomorrow (Thu 26 Apr) at 11am PT — Rafael, please send a calendar invite if that works. We need the draft rider + order-form language for internal routing by Mon 30 Apr.
